verify.howToSpotFake: How to spot a fake scholarship
verify.howToSpotFakeDesc: Before you apply, look for these warning signs. A quick check can help you avoid scams and protect your information.
verify.tip1Title: They ask you to pay to apply.
verify.tip1Desc: Be cautious when a scholarship asks for an upfront fee or payment.
verify.tip2Desc: Legitimate scholarships cannot promise that you will be selected before reviewing your application.
verify.tip3Title: The link only appears on social media.
verify.tip3Desc: Check whether the scholarship is listed on the university or organization’s official website.
verify.tip4Desc: Watch for shortened links, strange domains, spelling mistakes, or unfamiliar websites.
verify.tip5Title: They ask you to move to Telegram or WhatsApp.
verify.tip5Desc: Be careful when someone asks you to leave the official application process and continue through private messaging.
verify.tip6Title: They ask for sensitive information too early.
verify.tip6Desc: Think twice if they request bank details, ID numbers, or other sensitive information before you have even applied.
verify.tip7Title: They pressure you to act immediately.
verify.tip7Desc: Messages like “only 3 places left” or “closes in 24 hours” can be designed to rush your decision.
verify.tip8Title: They say you won something you never entered.
verify.tip8Desc: If you never applied or entered, an unexpected scholarship or prize message is a major warning sign.
verify.bestHabitDesc: Find the university or organization’s official website and look for the scholarship there. If you cannot find it through an official source, pause before you apply or share your information.
